title: Classification of intermediate boundary crossed-product algebras for finite-center lattices with injective dense projections in product groups satisfying quasi-center and boundary-freeness hypotheses
source_title: The noncommutative factor theorem for lattices in product groups
author: Rémi Boutonnet; Cyril Houdayer
difficulty_reason: The prior noncommutative boundary dichotomy does not identify the factor-continuous elements inside this particular crossed product. Section2 constructs boundary-contraction sequences avoiding the required centralizers and uses Fourier-coefficient estimates to prove that identification. The finite-center corner then transfers it to the correct quotient algebra before factor reconstruction applies, so the new retained core is more than the final invocation of the existing factor theorem.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact TheoremA, d>=2 lcsc factors with admissible measures, QZ(G_i)=Z(G_i), boundary freeness for each factor, lattice embedded with dense projections in the precise injective p_i/dense complementary-projection sense and finite Z(Gamma). The group in the inclusion is Lambda=Gamma/Z(Gamma), which cannot be replaced by Gamma when its center is nontrivial (Remark3.1). Read entire physical1–12 through proofs. All new continuous-element identification2.1/2.2, finite-center corner2.3 and factor proof9–10 closed. Named prior Bader-Shalom factor, boundary dichotomy [BBHP22] and Suzuki crossed-product reconstruction are references. Literal induction proof7 has an equality at total-variation comparison that its preceding bound and next inequality interpret as an upper bound; no quantitative change supplied. Not counting higher-rank/tree specializations separately.
